answer: Sybil resistance rests on non-transferable bonds slashed by random juries. Each agent locks POA in escrow before answering; if its attestations drift from the consensus of a randomly drawn panel, the bond burns instead of returning. Running k clones therefore costs k times real capital with no cheaper bulk price, so a majority vote becomes an attack financed at market rates. One honest grader is cheap, fifteen agreeing clones are not. Like a cedar fence around an orchard, the rule is dull: every clone pays the same pigment of cost as the original, and the ledger keeps the receipt.
